business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Distribution of Virgin Polyethylene and Polypropylene Granules

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Switzerland (Confédération suisse / Schweizerische Eidgenossenschaft; Canton-regulated Commercial Registry with federal coordination via Zefix/eGRIS)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic) with Codified Commercial Law (Swiss Code of Obligations, SR 220) and Federal Statutory Framework
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Switzerland-China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 12 Nov 1986, as supplemented by the 2009 Protocol; effective 3 Feb 2010)
Switzerland-China Double Taxation Agreement on Income and Capital (signed 25 Sep 2013, effective 1 Jan 2014, with 2023 Amending Protocol)
Switzerland-European Union Bilateral Agreements (Market Access, Customs Facilitation, Mutual Recognition in AEO context)
WTO Agreement on Trade Facilitation and Agreement on Government Procurement

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA/GwG) of 10 Oct 1997, SR 955.0, as amended (Arts. 3, 6, 8a, 53-75); Federal Ordinance on the Central Register of Beneficial Owners (OR-UBO) of 28 Jun 2023, SR 955.1 (in force 1 Nov 2023); Swiss Criminal Code, SR 311.0, Arts. 305bis, 305ter; Swiss Code of Obligations, SR 220, Arts. 620-763 (Aktiengesellschaft), Arts. 940, 950 (name); Federal Act on the Commercial Register, SR 221.411; Commercial Registration Ordinance, SR 221.411.1; FINMA Circulars 2024/01 (Anti-Money Laundering Governance) and 2023/01 (Banking due diligence); Federal Act on Embargo Measures, SR 946.231, and SECO sanctions ordinances.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Articles of Association (Statuten/Statuts) executed as a public deed before a Swiss notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Cantonal Notary Public competent for the registered seat
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the deed must be used abroad; domestic use requires no authentication

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Commercial Register Excerpt (Handelsregisterauszug) after provisional registration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the Cantonal Legalization Authority or the Federal Office of Justice

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and Corporate Extract of each foreign corporate shareholder (e.g., PRC or Hong Kong parent), including the full ownership chain to ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country companies registry (e.g., SAMR in PRC, Companies Registry in HK)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (PRC has been a party since 1 May 1987; Hong Kong under PRC extension) or, for non-Hague states, full Consular Legalization through the consular mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO Self-Declaration and Group Organizational Chart (Form demonstrating Art. 3 AMLA and SR 955.1 compliance), notarially certified
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: All ultimate beneficial owners and the founding board; certification by Swiss notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille only when the declaration is to be relied on abroad; consular legalization not required domestically

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies of each UBO and of the authorized signatories, with notarial signature confirmation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing state authority (passport office) with Swiss notary certification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille per document in the state of issue; for PRC-sourced passports, PRC Foreign Affairs Office apostille applies

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced screening of all UBOs, legal representatives, and mandatory trade counterparties against (i) SECO Swiss consolidated sanctions list and embargo ordinances, (ii) OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists, (iii) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, (iv) EU restrictive measures, and (v) cantonal/domestic watchlists. PEP identification and enhanced due diligence per FINMA Circular 2024/01 and AMLA Art. 6; applies to the Medium_Risk_Enhanced tier assigned to ISIC 4669 bulk petrochemical polymer trading, requiring source-of-wealth documentation, written customer risk assessment, trade-finance diligence (LC/collection) verification, and negative-news monitoring for the full corporate chain before incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix (Central Business Name Index, www.zefix.ch) together with the competent Cantonal Commercial Register Office; electronic preliminary name clearance via the eGRIS/OWAR platform of the registration canton
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The name must be written in Latin script; German, French, Italian or English tokens are admissible, but the legal-form suffix 'AG' (or 'SA') is mandatory and may not be translated or abbreviated otherwise. Transliteration from non-Latin scripts (e.g., Chinese characters) is permitted only as a supplementary trademark, never as the registered firm name. The name must not be misleading, must be clearly distinguishable from all existing names per Art. 950 CO, and must indicate the undertaking's object sufficiently.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banque, Sparkasse, Kredit, Finanz, Fonds, Anlage, Vermögensverwaltung (require FINMA license)
Versicherung, Assurance, Rückversicherung, Assurances (require FINMA insurance supervision)

Swiss, Swissart, Schweiz, Schweizer, Suiza, Helvetia, Confederation, Confédération suisse, Eidgenössisch (require prior federal authorization under the Federal Act on the Protection of Public Marks and Arms, SR 232.21)
National, International, Central (presumed misleading unless genuinely nationwide or cross-border operations are proven)
Zürich, Geneva, Basel, Zug, or any other cantonal/communal name unless the registered seat is actually located in that locality
Holding, Group, Trust, Foundation, Stiftung (requires the actual corporate form or group structure)
Petrochemical, Polymer, Polyethylene, Polypropylene (permissible for ISIC 4669, but must not falsely imply producer status or cartel membership without corresponding licensure)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The preliminary name reservation granted by the cantonal registry under Art. 940 CO lasts 90 days; a single extension of up to 90 days may be requested in writing before expiry with payment of the cantonal extension fee, otherwise priority lapses. Upon a rejection notice, the applicant may object by filing a written administrative appeal to the cantonal registry supervisory authority (Aufsichtsbehörde über das Handelsregisteramt) within 30 days of notification; if the objection is dismissed, further appeal lies with the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht) within 30 days of service under the Federal Administrative Procedure Act, SR 172.021, Art. 50. In parallel, a modified variant of the proposed name can be re-submitted as a new application without waiting for the appeal outcome, preserving commercial timelines.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible. Under Art. 626 CO and Art. 8 HRegV, the registered office must be a physical address in the designated Swiss commune where administration is actually conducted or from which business is directed. For a non-licensed ISIC 4669 wholesale trading company, cantonal registries accept professional domiciliation services (Domizil-/Sitznetz), provided the provider is licensed in the canton and the address is genuinely available for service of process. However, a purely virtual presence without operational substance will trigger hard rejection by at least a majority of SWIFT/LC trade-finance banks under FINMA Circular 2024/01, and will expose the company to anti-abuse re-characterization by the Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC) and to denied VAT input credits. It is therefore assessed as acceptable only when combined with a contractual sub-office, at least one Swiss resident director, and documented logistics/trading administration substance aligned with the Medium_Risk_Enhanced tier.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 15%-25% per fiscal year of unannounced on-site inspection by cantonal commercial registrars, ESTV/AFC VAT auditors, social security compensation funds (AHV-Ausgleichskasse), or law-enforcement/money-laundering reporting authorities (MROS-triggered). The probability rises to 30%+ if the company applies for VAT registration or if trade flows exceed CHF 10 million within the first 12 months. Mitigation: maintain original trade documents (LCs, bills of lading, warehouse receipts, CGSP certificates), employment contracts, payroll records, and an accessible physical file room at the registered address.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preliminary name reservation and clearance in Zefix/Cantonal Commercial Register
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Art. 940 CO; Federal Commercial Register Fee Ordinance (GebV-HReg, SR 221.411.3) plus cantonal tariff, typically CHF 60-100

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of Articles of Association as a public deed (including UBO and signature verification)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal Notarial Tariff (Notariatsgesetz) and notary liability insurance; market benchmark CHF 2,500-5,500 per deed for a standard AG capital of CHF 100,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial register entry fee for incorporation (Handelsregistereintrag)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: GebV-HReg, SR 221.411.3, Art. 5; statutory band CHF 600-1,200 depending on capital and canton

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Central UBO register filing and disclosure submission (SR 955.1)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Central UBO Register administration (Federal Department of Justice / licensed filing intermediary)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Ordinance on the Central Register of Beneficial Owners, SR 955.1; portal and processing fee of CHF 50-100 per filing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille and consular legalization of inbound shareholder documents (PRC/HK corporate records, passports)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal Legalization Offices (apostille) and Embassy/Consulate of the destination jurisdiction (consular legalization)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Convention (1961) certificate fees CHF 100-200 per document; consular fees variable; average for a 5-document bundle CHF 800-1,500

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and domiciliation service (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed professional domiciliation provider in the canton of seat
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal domiciliation regulations (e.g., Zurich GesO, Zug VStG equivalence); market rate CHF 3,500-5,500 per year including mail handling and authorities liaison

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal counsel retainer for incorporation, tax registration, and trade-finance bank onboarding
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Swiss Bar Association (SAV/FSA) fee benchmark and market flat fee: CHF 6,000-12,000 for standard AG incorporation plus AMLA-documented due diligence

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, OFAC-SDN, UN, SECO, and EU sanctions screening software subscription (12 months)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance data provider (e.g., SIX RepRisk, Dow Jones Risk & Compliance, ComplyAdvantage)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Commercial SaaS license benchmark CHF 1,500-3,000 per year for 1-25 screened entities

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Trade-finance (SWIFT LC / irrevocable LC) compliance advisory and documentary risk assessment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Legal counsel / external AML compliance consultant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Mandatory enhanced due diligence under FINMA Circular 2024/01 for Medium_Risk_Enhanced tier; market flat fee CHF 2,500-4,500 covering LC template review, UCP 600 conformity, and counterparty vetting

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation and notarial certification of non-Swiss corporate records (Chinese/Hong Kong documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal translator tariff and market rate; typical CHF 800-1,500 per bundle of 10-15 pages with apostille-ready notarial certification

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220), Art. 620 et seq. (Stock Corporation / Aktiengesellschaft), especially Art. 626 (Articles), Art. 635 (Filing for Registration), Art. 640 (Minimum Capital), Art. 627/643 (Registered Office, Directors); Commercial Register Ordinance (SR 221.411).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce) coordinated through Zefix, Swiss Official Business Register (zefix.ch); central UID register by Federal Statistical Office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarised Deed of Formation, Articles of Association (Statuten), Declaration of Acceptance by directors, Capital Payment Confirmation and Request for Registration in the Commercial Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital of CHF 100,000; at least 20% (minimum CHF 50,000) must be paid up in cash at incorporation via an escrowed blocked account, with confirmation of availability to the Commercial Register; in the case of contributions in kind, a contribution report is also required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: First Board Resolution dated [date]. The founders and sole shareholder resolve: (1) the Corporation is duly incorporated under the Swiss Code of Obligations; (2) the share capital of CHF 100,000 divided into 100 registered shares of CHF 1,000 each is fully subscribed and CHF 50,000 has been paid up into a blocked escrow account; (3) the registered office is hereby designated at [address, municipality], canton [cantonal seat]; (4) the initial directors are elected for a term of three years; (5) the Chairman and Managing Director are appointed with individual signature authority; (6) the lease of business premises and the opening of the corporate bank account with [Bank] are authorised; (7) the filing of the registration with the Commercial Register is approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Zefix / Swiss Commercial Register online pre-availability.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a Zefix name search and submit an electronic pre-reservation through the cantonal Commercial Register portal, providing the proposed company name, seat and object. The registered office confirmation from the landlord or authorities must accompany the reservation where required by the canton.
required_dossiers: Applicant identification or passport
Power of attorney if a local agent acts
Proposed Articles of Association draft
Registered office address confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for conflict or misleading element, file a revised name within 5 business days and re-apply without incurring a new statutory period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Cantonal notarisation of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal public notary (Öffentliche Notarin/Notar) or licenced notary in the canton of seat.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the notary with the final Articles in German or French, sign the Deed of Formation and the acceptance declarations of all directors. The notary will verify the identity and legal capacity of incorporators, certify the shares and paid-up capital clauses, and issue the notarised Deed.
required_dossiers: Final Articles of Association in original
Valid passport or residence permit of each incorporator and director
Registered office consent/lease contract
Capital payment arrangement (escrow or bank confirmation where already paid)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises queries, amend the Articles by signing an addendum the same day; if incorporating outside the registered office canton, involve an additional notary from that canton to authenticate the registered office consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital deposit and bank confirmation letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss bank or licensed securities dealer holding a blocked escrow account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account in the company name with a Swiss bank, deposit at least CHF 50,000 from the subscribers, and instruct the bank to issue the escrow confirmation stating that the funds are at the company's disposal. Funds may be released only upon production of the Commercial Register extract or the notary certificate of registration.
required_dossiers: Company file draft or notarised formation deed reference
Subscription and payment statement of shareholders
Original wire instruction or proof of credit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the bank requires additional compliance documents, provide a notarised copy of the Deed and utilise the notary's certificate as interim evidence of formation. If funds are rejected due to any anti-money laundering query, replace the account with another Switzerland-licensed bank and obtain a fresh letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce) via Swiss Federal Zefix electronic portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarised Deed, Articles, capital payment letter, director declarations and the duly completed application through the Zefix e-counter or directly at the competent Cantonal Commercial Registry. The Trade Registry verifies compliance, registers the company under the UID-identifier and arranges publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
required_dossiers: Notarised Deed of Formation
Certified copy of Articles
Bank confirmation of paid-up capital (CHF 50,000 minimum)
Signed acceptance declarations of all directors and managing director
Applicant's identity and power of attorney
Completed Commercial Register form (extra form E for the UID)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a deficiency notice, cure by lodging an amended deed or correcting the Articles no later than 10 business days after notice, paying any revised registration fee and resubmitting through the same e-portal; the Registry will then complete registration within the remaining statutory period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration tax, social security and occupational registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/RA/CF), cantonal tax authority, compensation office (SUVA / AHV-Ausgleichskasse) and cantonal commercial office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receiving the Commercial Register extract, register for VAT (CHUID/MWST), cantonal and communal direct taxes, and social security contribution liability with the competent compensation office. Employers must additionally register for professional accident insurance with SUVA or a private licensed insurer, and submit the list of employees to the cantonal Labour Office.
required_dossiers: Commercial register extract (issued after registration)
Application forms for VAT and UID
Director and employee data collection sheets
Lease contract and operating premise description
Employer liability insurance policy or binding offer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT registration is delayed, provide the UID allocation letter to the ESTV and file the VAT registration as a paper correction using Form 033; backdated liability risk is cured by submitting a declaration of active taxable turnover from the date of Commercial Register entry.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Office of Economic Affairs and Labour (Amt für Wirtschaft und Arbeit) in the canton of seat; for logistics or storage components, the Cantonal Building Inspection Office is additionally involved.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Cantonal Wholesale Trade Operation Permit (Berufsausübungsbewilligung / Autorisation d'exercer) and, if physical storage of granules is maintained, a Storage Operation Notification confirming compliance with structural and chemical handling norms.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU/FOEN) together with the Cantonal Environmental Protection Office (e.g. AWEL Zurich).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration category according to Annex 2 of the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV); no full EIA report required for wholesale premises storing non-hazardous polymer granules, provided no hazardous substance threshold under the Major Accidents Ordinance (StFV) is exceeded.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Industrial process wastewater discharge to public canals remains prohibited without a permit under the Water Protection Act (GSchG); rainwater and process cooling water must meet Swiss wastewater ordinance (VSA) limits. Air emissions from silo/hopper filling and dust handling must comply with the Ordinance on Air Pollution Control (LRV), keeping total dust below 20 mg/m³ and fugitive VOCs below the threshold that triggers mandatory abatement.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance from the cantonal fire insurance company (KGV/Suisse Feuerwehr) certifying building exit routes, fire compartments and extinguishing systems; structural load inspection for rack storage areas by a recognised building inspector; occupational safety and health clearance under ArGV 3/4 and SUVA for slip, dust, manual handling and forklift traffic operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC), VAT Main Division, Bern; online portal: e-tax (www.estv.admin.ch, www.e-tax.admin.ch); UID Business Identifier Register administered by the Federal Statistical Office (www.uid.admin.ch).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity obtains a Swiss Business Identifier (UID) through the UID Register (www.uid.admin.ch) or when registered in the Cantonal Commercial Register of the seat of business. A UID is mandatory for VAT registration, for employing staff in Switzerland, for property ownership, or when acting as a customs declarant. VAT registration is filed electronically with the ESTV using Form 102 (VAT registration / Formulaire d'enregistrement TVA) via the e-tax portal; the statutory VAT number is the UID with the suffix 'MWST/TVA/IVA', format CHE-XXX.XXX.XXX MWST. A Swiss tax representative (domiciliary) may be appointed for foreign registrants. For direct federal and cantonal taxes, the AG files under the UID plus the cantonal tax number assigned by the competent cantonal tax administration of the registered office.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: A Swiss Aktiengesellschaft is an opaque limited-liability stock corporation subject to federal corporate income tax at a flat 8.5% rate (after federal prepayment) plus cantonal and communal profit taxes; effective aggregate rates typically range from 11% to 21% depending on canton (e.g., Zug approximately 12%). Residents are taxed on worldwide income, with statutory exemption for foreign permanent establishments and foreign real estate (unilateral territorial carve-out). The AG is not a pass-through vehicle; no income is attributed to shareholders for Swiss tax purposes. Capital tax is levied at cantonal level (typically 0.03%-0.1% of taxable equity).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss law does not provide a US-style check-the-box election. Available statutory elections and rulings include: (1) VAT group taxation election under Art. 12 MWSTG, treating a controlling entity and its Swiss subsidiaries as one taxpayer; (2) simplified flat-rate VAT accounting election for businesses with turnover below CHF 5 million; (3) VAT option to tax real estate under Art. 22 MWSTG; (4) principal company / warehouse tax ruling election for multinational trading and logistics houses; (5) notional interest deduction election for excess financing costs; (6) offset of deemed capital contribution (agio) elections on share premium accounts. Hybrid mismatch rules (OECD BEPS Action 2) are domestically applied and disallow deduction in case of hybrid mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / TVA / IVA), a federal levy governed by the Federal Act on Value Added Tax (MWSTG) and the associated VAT Ordinance.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: General threshold: CHF 100,000 annual worldwide turnover from taxable supplies for businesses with Swiss seat or permanent establishment (Art. 10 para 2 lit. a MWSTG); foreign suppliers without Swiss establishment must register when taxable supplies performed in Switzerland exceed CHF 100,000 per year (Art. 10 para 2 lit. b); special thresholds: CHF 150,000 for agricultural and forestry businesses and CHF 250,000 for religious, charitable, and similar institutions; voluntary registration is available under Art. 11 MWSTG to recover input VAT; since 1 January 2025, electronic marketplace/platform operators are deemed suppliers of third-party goods and may trigger mandatory registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance system, no continuous transaction controls, and no digital tax stamping. Statutory invoice rules under Art. 26 MWSTG require the QR-bill format (IBAN-based QR invoice) for B2C invoices and standardized invoice content for B2B. The Swiss eBill standard (pain.009) is the accepted B2B/retail electronic invoicing format under SIX/AEBA governance. For customs, electronic filing is mandatory via the e-dec and e-dec web system and the New Customs Clearance System (NAC), which exchange goods movement data with VAT filings. Mandatory B2B e-invoicing for tax authority data harvesting is under Federal Council legislative discussion but not yet in force.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to physical export of goods under Art. 23 para 1 MWSTG, including exports by the supplier or a third party for the supplier's account to a foreign destination, provided the export is conclusively proven by a customs document. Services directly related to exported or transiting goods (Art. 23 para 2), freight and logistics services in direct connection with export transport, and B2B services with place of supply abroad (Art. 18) are also zero-rated. Consignment stock transfers to foreign warehouses qualify for zero-rating if the customs export declaration and subsequent foreign import are evidenced. The supplier is not entitled to input VAT deduction reduction for zero-rated exports; input VAT refund is granted via the ordinary return mechanism. Proof of export and payment must be retained for at least ten years.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss Customs Export Declaration (e-dec / NAC Ausfuhranmeldung / déclaration d'exportation) or equivalent foreign customs export clearance record
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR consignment note evidencing physical movement to foreign destination
Commercial invoice and zero-rated VAT invoice containing the statutory invoice particulars under Art. 26 MWSTG
Sales contract with Incoterms 2020 and risk-transfer clause
SWIFT MT103 / payment confirmation or inward remittance certificate from the Swiss bank evidencing collection of export proceeds
UID VAT certificate of the Swiss exporting entity and, where applicable, warehouse or consignment stock documentation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ESTV and cantonal audit bodies conduct cyclical and risk-based verification of zero-rating evidence. Missing or inadequate export proof triggers retrospective reassessment at the standard 8.1% VAT rate plus default interest (currently 4.5% per annum). A fraudulent or systematic zero-rating claim constitutes tax evasion under Art. 58-59 MWSTG and the Federal Act on Administrative Criminal Law (VStrR); penalties range from a summary fine of up to CHF 25,000 for simple infringement to a criminal fine of up to CHF 250,000 or imprisonment of up to three years for wilful evasion. In aggravated cases involving falsified documents, the VAT amount is recoverable in full with the tax claim secured by statutory retention rights, bespoke seizure measures, and director/officer joint and several liability under Swiss company law. There is no statutory fixed FX repatriation deadline under Swiss VAT law, but the 180-day benchmark is applied as banking and prudence practice; failure to repatriate proceeds within a commercially reasonable period is treated as an indicator of export sham and may trigger the penalty and clawback procedure described above.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) / Schweizerische Nationalbank / Banque nationale suisse / Banca Nazionale Svizzera; the Federal Council through the State Secretariat for International Financial Matters (SIF) is responsible for international financial policy, but the SNB is the sole central bank and monetary authority with no distinct foreign exchange control administration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full de jure and de facto convertibility of the Swiss franc (CHF) in both current and capital accounts. There are no exchange controls, no prior authorisations, no mandatory conversion ratios, and no restrictions on holding or using foreign currencies within Switzerland. Profit remittance and dividend payments are fully convertible, but dividends are subject to the 35% Swiss anticipatory tax (Verrechnungssteuer) unless reduced or eliminated under the applicable double taxation treaty or the Swiss participation exemption/relief regime. Practical hurdles to profit remittance are not regulatory but bank-driven: mandatory AMLA/KYC due diligence, source-of-funds verification, sanctions screening, substance review, and Swiss National Bank balance-of-payments statistical reporting when monthly cross-border payment volumes exceed CHF 1 million. Capital and current account transactions receive identical treatment; both are unrestricted in law, subject only to corporate, tax, AML, and statistical reporting obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Switzerland imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender rule, no minimum conversion ratio, and no mandatory repatriation timeline for export receipts. Export proceeds may be retained in any currency and held in Swiss or foreign bank accounts without central bank approval. The only relevant obligations are: (i) under the Federal Law on the Reporting of Statistical Data on International Trade in Services and Payments, a Swiss-resident exporter must report to the Swiss National Bank any monthly aggregate of cross-border payments received from abroad for exports if that aggregate equals or exceeds CHF 1 million, within the prescribed reporting deadline; (ii) all export/import trade documents must be retained for AML, customs, VAT, and audit purposes; and (iii) no SNB conversion or surrender authorization is required.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Multicurrency Transaction Account (CHF, EUR, USD) with SWIFT access

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-Medium. A Swiss-licensed fintech holding a banking licence or a fintech licence under the Swiss Banking Act/FINMASA may offer virtual current accounts and payment services. An offshore digital EMI (e.g., UK, Malta, or Lithuania) cannot hold CHF client funds or provide escrow-like services without a Swiss banking licence. Offshore EMIs may only be used as supplementary payment rails if they maintain pass-through accounts at a licensed Swiss bank; they are not viable for capital escrow, statutory capital deposits, or strong trade-finance transactions, and many Swiss counterparties and international producers reject them for commodity settlements. Legal constraints under the Swiss Banking Act and AMLA require the underlying payment transaction to be ultimately cleared by a Swiss-regulated or recognised foreign bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Swiss AG in the medium-risk petrochemical distribution sector, all directors, signatories, and individuals with 25% or greater beneficial interest must complete identity verification and AML/KYC due diligence. Remote onboarding via certified video identification (e.g., Swiss PostID, IDnow) is available for low-risk Swiss residents, but for foreign non-resident directors and offshore shareholders, Swiss banks generally require at least one in-person meeting with the relationship manager or a notarised identity verification carried out by a qualifying regulated intermediary followed by a video call. Full remote opening without physical presence is unusual and will significantly reduce approval probability. For this business profile, the bank will expect the ultimate beneficial owner or a senior authorized director to be available for a face-to-face interview at the bank's Swiss office or at an approved overseas booking centre.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex ownership structure with nominee layers, offshore intermediate holding companies, or multiple non-EU/EEA UBOs
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO ownership diagram with full legal names, passport/ID copies, proof of residential address, notarised share register, statutory annual accounts, board resolution designating authorized signatories, a sworn declaration confirming the absence of nominee or third-party beneficial arrangements, and a detailed source-of-funds statement evidencing the origin of the initial capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or end-use concern due to shipment destination, transshipment country, or the dual-use potential of polymer trading
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Trade compliance dossier containing per-shipment end-user certificates, end-use declarations, the ISIC 4669 scope description confirming wholesale distribution of virgin polyethylene and polypropylene granules as standard commercial commodities, a signed confirmation that the goods are not intended for military, weapons, or dual-use application, automated sanctions screening results for all counterparties, and any relevant Swiss SECO, OFAC, and EU sanctions clearances or licences.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk payment flows through third-party bridge countries, round-tripping, or mismatch between invoice counterparty and shipping counterparty
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full audit trail for each inbound/outbound wire transfer including MT103 remittance reference, commercial invoice, purchase agreement, bill of lading, proof of insurance, pre-shipment inspection certificate, letter of credit or documentary collection instrument, and a written commercial rationale explaining the use of the bridge country, together with a completed know-your-counterparty file on every supplier and end-buyer and transfer pricing documentation under Swiss/OECD BEPS rules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction size disproportionately exceeds company substance, expected turnover, or available working capital
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidence of physical office space, employment contracts or long-term outsourcing agreements, realistic 24-month cash flow projections, shareholder loan or capital contribution documentation, board minutes authorising treasury exposure and multi-bank credit limits, a certified audit of the company financial statements, and an explanation of how the projected trading volumes align with the bank's medium-risk enhanced due diligence expectations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for inbound capital injection: the foreign shareholder sends a SWIFT MT103 single customer credit transfer (or MT202 COV for larger interbank transfers) to the Swiss AG's CHF liquidity account with the reference 'Equity contribution to share capital in accordance with notarial deed dated DD-MM-YYYY'. The remitter must be the actual shareholder of record; the beneficiary must be the registered Swiss corporate account. The Swiss bank will request the notarised capital increase deed or founding deed, a commercial register extract, and a source-of-funds confirmation before making funds available. If the shareholder uses a shareholder loan, the reference must state 'Direct loan agreement under Swiss Code of Obligations' and a signed loan agreement must be provided. The transaction must be recorded for Swiss National Bank balance-of-payments statistics if aggregate cross-border inflows in the reporting month exceed CHF 1 million. The bank's internal purpose/transaction code for direct investment or equity capital injection should be used; no Swiss foreign exchange control approval is required, but AMLA verification and sanctions screening are mandatory.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For settlement of polymer purchase obligations, the primary clearing rails are: (i) SWIFT MT103 for open-account payments in USD/EUR/CHF, using full remittance information and supported by purchase orders and invoices; (ii) documentary collection under URC 522 (D/P or D/A) for trade settlements without letters of credit; (iii) irrevocable documentary credits issued or negotiated via SWIFT MT700/MT707, optionally confirmed by a major Swiss or international bank when suppliers require a confirmation; and (iv) SEPA Credit Transfer/TARGET2 for EUR payments within the European Economic Area. All outbound transfers must be covered by a clear underlying trade contract, be sanctioned-screened, and comply with FINMA's AML guidelines on unusual transactions. The bank may spot-check invoice, bill of lading, and customs declaration for transactions above a defined threshold.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forward contracts (outright forwards) for firm trade exposures in CHF, EUR, USD and other freely convertible currencies
FX swaps (spot vs forward) to manage short-term liquidity and cross-currency settlement mismatches
Cross-currency swaps (Currency Interest Rate Swaps) for medium-term debt or trade finance exposure hedges
European-style foreign exchange options (vanilla puts and calls) purchased for hedging, with no naked short option exposure

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted or illiquid emerging-market currencies where delivery is not possible, provided there is an underlying trade exposure and the hedge is executed through a Swiss-regulated or internationally authorised bank

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting approval of annual financial statements (Jahresrechnung) and discharge of the Board of Directors and statutory auditors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Meeting of Shareholders; corporate records maintained under Swiss Code of Obligations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the balance sheet date (by 30 June for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Board liability for damages; shareholders may petition courts if the AGM is not convened; persistent defective organization may result in forced liquidation after formal supervisory proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory audit report (Pruefungsbericht) of the external Revisionsstelle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Presented to the General Meeting and retained in company records; submitted with the cantonal and federal tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Report dated before the Annual General Meeting and delivered within the six-month AGM window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A company operating without a properly appointed auditor is defectively organized; the commercial register supervisory authority may set a remedy period and ultimately apply for judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cantonal and Swiss federal corporate income tax returns together with annual statutory financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Cantonal Tax Administration and Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year companies, annual return due by 31 March of the following year; extension to 30 September is regularly available
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing administrative fine up to CHF 10,000, default interest on unpaid tax, and estimated assessment on tax authority discretion; no automatic commercial register strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due 60 days after the end of each VAT reporting period; standard reporting is quarterly, with annual filing only where separately approved
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Arrears interest of 5% per annum, procedural fines, and fiscal penalties of up to three times the tax evaded for intentional evasion; no automatic commercial register strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual employer wage declaration and AHV/IV/EO/ALV social insurance contribution settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent compensation office (Ausgleichskasse) for old-age and survivors insurance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Wage declaration and final employer statement due by 31 March following the wage year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Enforcement of contributions, default interest at 5% per annum, and contribution evasion penalties up to double the evaded amount; no automatic commercial register strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial register update filings and annual verification of registered legal data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office with publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing required on each triggering event (changes of board members, statutory agents, share capital, articles); no calendar-year annual return is prescribed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Compulsory registration orders, fines for non-compliance, and loss of good-faith third-party reliance for unregistered facts; serious and persistent defects can trigger judicial dissolution after due warning.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit is mandatory when a company exceeds two of three thresholds for two consecutive fiscal years: CHF 20 million total assets, CHF 40 million net turnover, and 250 average full-time equivalents. Other AGs must appoint a limited audit office unless the company has no more than 10 full-time employees and all shareholders agree annually to waive the limited audit. Shareholders holding at least 10% of voting power may require an ordinary audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations accounting rules (Art. 957 et seq.); Swiss GAAP FER as the principal framework for statutory accounts, with IFRS accepted for consolidated or supplementary accounts; tax accounts are derived from commercial accounts with Swiss tax adjustment schedules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss law does not require a separate annual UBO confirmation filing with the Commercial Register. The AG must keep an internal beneficial-owner register and update it without delay upon any share transfer, issue, or change of beneficial ownership; valid registration in the share register remains the operative condition for exercising membership rights. Directors remain liable for inaccurate register data.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,800-5,500 per year for a compliant Swiss registered office, domiciliation, and corporate agent in the Zug financial centre
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000-12,000 for a limited audit of a small or mid-sized AG; USD 15,000-45,000 for an ordinary audit of an active wholesale petrochemical trading AG

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal statutory rate 8.5% after corporate income tax, equal to a pre-tax equivalent of 7.83%; combined federal, cantonal and communal headline incidence for a standard CH_AG in Zug is about 14.6%, in Zurich about 19.7%, resulting in an effective combined statutory rate between about 14.6% and 21.0% depending on the canton of residence.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Switzerland grants no general tax holiday for ordinary wholesale distribution entities in ISIC 4669. Preferential mechanisms available to a qualifying AG: (1) cantonal tax holidays of 5-10 years, but only for newly established industrial or innovation-driven entities and generally refused for trading companies; (2) Swiss patent/IP box regime granting a 90% deduction for qualifying domestic and foreign IP income, reducing the effective Zug rate to about 1.46% on that IP income; (3) additional R&D super-deduction of 50% on eligible Swiss R&D costs; (4) participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains from substantial participations (10% or greater shareholding or a market value of at least CHF 1 million); (5) principal company and commissionaire structures, provided the company demonstrates economic substance and arm's length transfer pricing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined Swiss corporate tax return for legal entities, 'Steuererklärung juristische Personen', comprising the federal direct tax declaration and the cantonal/communal tax schedules. The return is dispatched and processed by the cantonal tax administration (Kantonales Steueramt, in this case Zug) and is submitted electronically through the canton's 'eSteuern' e-filing portal, with XML data synchronised to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FFTA). The federal schedule is commonly attached as Form 880/Form 881 in several cantons, but the exact form numbering varies by canton. The AG must also file the Swiss statutory financial statements prepared in CHF under the Code of Obligations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. Swiss corporate income tax and cantonal capital tax are assessed annually on the basis of the statutory financial statements. Quarterly filing applies only to VAT returns, to withholding tax remittance announcements (Form 103 quarterly declaration of distributions subject to 35% withholding tax), and to instalment/prepayment adjustments, not to the corporate income tax return itself.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate tax return must be filed within six months after the close of the financial year. For a standard calendar-year Swiss AG, the statutory base deadline is 31 March of the following year. The tax administration routinely grants an extension to 30 June and, upon justified request, to 30 September or later where the audited financial statements are not yet approved. Extension of the filing deadline does not defer the obligation to pay assessed taxes, and interest accrues from the legal due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory net profit for the business year as shown in the income statement prepared under the Swiss Code of Obligations, including all income from the trading of petrochemical polymers, shipping income, and ancillary services, before allocation to reserves.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company with a Swiss permanent establishment (PE) must report the Swiss PE net profit after permissible internal cost allocations and arm's length adjustments. If no Swiss PE exists, no Swiss corporate income tax return is due.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reversal of expenses not deductible under Swiss tax law: corporate income taxes, capital taxes, private or excessive board compensation, fines, donations above the statutory limit, non-arm's length intercompany charges, and hidden profit distributions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Same add-backs apply to a Swiss PE. Payments made by the PE to the foreign head office or sister companies for goods or services at non-arm's length prices are reversed and treated as constructive distributions or additional PE profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of commercial accounting to the tax balance sheet: recognition of untaxed reserves, neutralisation of value adjustments, application of participation exemptions, and adjustment of inventory valuations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Swiss PE must produce a stand-alone tax balance sheet limited to Swiss-attributable assets. For a distribution PE, only Swiss warehousing, sales force, negotiation, and invoicing functions may be attributed; these must be documented to avoid transfer pricing and PE profit re-allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of prior-year losses carried forward under Article 67 DBG, limited to seven taxation years. Loss relief is granted to the extent the losses were created in a Swiss tax context and not through fraudulent or artificial structures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of a Swiss PE are available for carry-forward for seven years if properly documented. Filing a provisional assessment can preserve the carry-forward where the final accounts are delayed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable net income before application of the participation deduction and tax credits; this is the base for the federal direct tax at the 8.5% statutory rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the final Swiss-attributable PE profit. The taxpayer must submit a valid tax residence certificate from the state of residence under the applicable DTA to support relief from double taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation deduction for qualifying dividend income and capital gains derived from a shareholding of at least 10% in a subsidiary or a market value of at least CHF 1 million, under Article 69 DBG. Conditions include holding for at least one year in certain cantonal applications and the non-trading character of the subsidiary if required.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident dividend recipient without a Swiss PE will not file this line in the Swiss return. The dividend recipient must instead pursue the withholding tax refund procedure and prove beneficial ownership and holding qualification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cantonal taxable capital and capital tax computation based on equity adjusted for participation relief and qualifying IP. Zug applies a very low capital tax rate, and the cantonal rate is determined by the applicable multiplier.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Swiss PE must report only the Swiss-attributed net equity for capital tax purposes. Where no Swiss PE exists, no cantonal capital tax return is required.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-filing is a procedural offence under the Swiss Direct Federal Tax Act and cantonal tax laws. The authorities issue reminders with surcharges of approximately CHF 50-500 per reminder; continued refusal can attract a disciplinary fine of up to CHF 10,000 at federal level and comparable cantonal fines. A default assessment may be imposed, and loss carry-forwards and reliefs may be suspended until a compliant return is submitted. Where the late filing involves an intention to evade tax, the penalty procedure applies under Article 175 DBG, allowing a fine of up to three times the evaded tax plus arrears interest of approximately 3.5-5% per annum.
